A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RGNMR study. Their algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original matrix-recovery simulations, runtime measurements, and background extraction from the Hall video in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GNMR comparisons, diagonal-band sampling experiments, noisy recovery sweeps, and accuracy measurements across matrix sizes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the Gauss–Newton update, outlier removal, binary search for the corruption count, and noise-dependent stopping rule are retained. Expanded explanations do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds diagonal-band observation patterns, extending coverage beyond uniform and power-law sampling. The synthetic matrix-completion task and Hall video dataset remain unchanged; additive noise was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: New Figure 5 evaluates the nonrobust GNMR method directly against RGNMR; v1 discussed GNMR without reporting this comparison. The comparator membership in retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments use 500×500 matrices for the GNMR and diagonal-band tests and fixed Gaussian noise σ=10^-6 for condition-number and oversampling sweeps. Existing experiments retain their matrix-generation procedures, metrics, failure threshold, and baseline parameters.

E4.justification: The supplementary analyses substantially expand: Figure 5 tests the value of outlier handling, Figure 8 examines structured missingness, Figures 10–11 examine noise jointly with conditioning and sample scarcity, and Figure 14 adds accuracy versus matrix size. These questions extend beyond v1's existing robustness and runtime analyses.

E5.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their stated independent-realization counts and uncertainty reporting, including ±1.96 SE failure-probability bars. Added experiments reuse these practices; no new statistical estimation procedure, significance test, or seed policy is reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the added analyses. Figure 5 shows GNMR failing at every positive corruption level plotted while RGNMR succeeds; Figure 8 reports RGNMR's advantage under diagonal-band sampling. Figures 10–11 add noisy recovery results, and Figure 14 adds accuracy across matrix sizes. Matched earlier results, including the runtime curves, are retained.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–3, Theorems 3.1–3.2, the recovery guarantees in Table 1, and the mathematical arguments in Appendices C–F remain unchanged. Added explanatory prose introduces no new theorem, proof, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central recovery, robustness, and theoretical-advantage claims are retained. The added abstract sentence highlights corruption-count estimation and its possible use by other methods, both already stated in v1 Section 2.1 and Remark 2.2.

C2.justification: New Remark 2.1 explains the recovery obstruction when outlier removal leaves fewer than r observations in a row or column. Section 5 newly acknowledges greater computational demands than some competing methods and attributes them to solving large linear systems. Existing theoretical limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v1 promises public code upon publication; v2 supplies a stated public GitHub location for MATLAB/Python implementations and declares open experimental code in its checklist. Appendix B also documents diagonal-band construction. Existing hardware and baseline-setting disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wu et al. (2025) and Lejun et al. (2025) for application context and Okatani et al. (2011) for structured sampling. The central positioning against existing RMC methods and their theoretical guarantees remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives localized rewrites and expanded remarks. Limitations move into Section 5, and acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added. Some edits introduce visible wording errors, including 'stpdf' in place of 'steps'.

P2.justification: v2 adds four two-panel figures: 5, 8, 10, and 11. The former runtime-only Figure 10 becomes Figure 14 with an additional accuracy panel. This substantially expands the visual evidence; other figures retain their plotted content, with renumbering and limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: The added controls and robustness analyses strengthen empirical support, while the explicit computational limitation and public-code access information improve transparency. These are incremental gains because v1 already contained the method, proofs, and extensive experiments. Newly introduced wording errors slightly weaken presentation but do not outweigh those benefits.
